title: The Splitter allocates surplus between SKY accumulation and USDS staking rewards, currently sending all of it to accumulation
content:
A.3.5.2.1 describes the Splitter Module as splitting funds received from the Surplus Buffer "between accumulating SKY and paying USDS rewards to SKY stakers." A.3.5.2.1.1.2 defines the `burn` parameter as the percentage of each transfer sent to the Flapper contract (which accumulates SKY), with "the remainder of each transfer" going to the staker rewards contract.

So a single parameter arbitrates between two competing claims on the same revenue: retiring supply (which benefits all SKY holders passively) versus paying yield to the subset that stakes. A.3.5.2 records `burn` at 100%, meaning staker rewards are currently unfunded by this engine.

A second constraint couples the two halves of the mechanism: the LSEV2-SKY-A USDS `rewardsDuration` "must be set such that it is equal to the `splitter.hop` parameter." Because `hop` is the interval between transfers into the Splitter (A.3.5.2.1.1.1), matching the reward stream's duration to it makes each incoming lot stream out exactly until the next lot arrives — the reward rate is smooth and gapless by construction rather than by monitoring.

That coupling is why A.3.5.2.3 permits `rewardsDuration` to track `hop` "without requiring prior governance authorization": it is a derived value, and letting it drift out of sync would break the stream, not express a policy choice.
description: The burn parameter is the fraction routed to the Flapper contract; the remainder funds USDS rewards for SKY stakers, and the reward stream's duration must equal the transfer interval.
